title: Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference
gist: NVIDIA follows its Nemotron 3.5 Parse document model release with ~19M open synthetic training examples (charts, tables, multilingual OCR), an SFT + GRPO-based RLVR fine-tuning recipe, and a DFlash2 speculative decoder that lifts throughput up to 7.62x. RLVR cut looping outputs ~77% and raised overall score from 66.24 to 71.38, while architecture changes put Parse 3.5 at 4.5-6.9x Parse 2.0 throughput on an H200.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Parse is a compact document model that converts page images into structured data — reading-order content, content classes, bounding boxes, and structured records for tables and charts — for RAG and agent pipelines.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is pushing into the enterprise document-ingestion layer for agentic/RAG workloads, competing with OCR/IDP vendors.

insights.claim: NVIDIA open-sourced three Nemotron Parse 3.5 training datasets: Synthetic Charts V1 (9.98M examples), Synthetic Tables V1 (1M), and OCR Synthetic Multilingual v2 (7.9M), each with images, annotations, generation documentation and training format.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: Releasing ~19M open examples commoditises document-AI training data and lowers barriers for fine-tuned parsers on NVIDIA's stack.

insights.claim: Nemotron Parse 3.5's gains on hard charts and tables were largely powered by synthetic data generation: rendering chart/table variations with known ground truth and training the model to reverse the rendering, enabling it to infer unlabelled bar values from axes and bar height.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: Synthetic render-and-invert data is a scalable moat-reducer for document AI — proprietary labelled corpora matter less.
insights.quote: These advancements have been largely powered by synthetic data generation
insights.locator: This latest version of Parse significantly extends

insights.claim: NVIDIA trained Nemotron Parse 3.5 in two phases: supervised fine-tuning to establish page-reading capability, then reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) via GRPO, rewarding correct series/values, usable structure and finishing without repetition.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: SFT-for-capability, RLVR-for-reliability is becoming the standard recipe for production structured-extraction models.
insights.quote: SFT teaches the capability; RLVR improves consistency
insights.locator: SFT teaches the capability; RLVR improves consistency

insights.claim: Verifier-based rewards let a document model find any of several valid representations of a difficult page rather than matching one exact token sequence, while discouraging looping and unfinished output.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: Verifiable-reward RL suits tasks with multiple correct outputs — a broadly transferable approach beyond document parsing.
insights.locator: A difficult page can have several valid representations

insights.claim: In a matched development-checkpoint comparison, GRPO cut loop-flagged outputs from 126 to 29 pages (~77% fewer), outputs hitting the 9,000-token limit from 185 to 35, and raised overall score from 66.24 to 71.38, including +5.18 points on tables and +4.15 on charts.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: RL's biggest payoff is reliability (fewer runaway generations), which directly cuts inference waste in production pipelines.
insights.locator: The matched comparison shows the benefit

insights.claim: Nemotron Parse 3.5 replaces Parse 2.0's fixed 2048x1664 canvas and encoder-decoder cross-attention with NaViT dynamic rectangular inputs, compressed visual tokens fed as a causal prefix, and GQA-8 decoder attention (16 query heads, 8 key/value heads) to cut attention-cache memory.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: Decoder-only VLM designs with compressed visual prefixes are displacing encoder-decoder OCR architectures for efficiency.
insights.locator: Faster inference through architecture and DFlash2

insights.claim: NVIDIA's DFlash2 speculator uses a small draft model proposing up to 32 tokens that Nemotron Parse verifies together, averaging about 14 accepted draft tokens — roughly 15 output tokens of progress per verification step.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: Structured, predictable outputs (like document markup) are ideal for aggressive speculative decoding, sharply lowering cost per page.

insights.claim: On one H200 in BF16, DFlash2 raised Nemotron Parse 3.5 throughput 7.62x at concurrency 1 and 1.52x at concurrency 512; at 512, Parse 3.5 reaches 13.48 pages/s without speculation and 20.44 with DFlash2, versus 2.98 for Parse 2.0 (4.53x and 6.86x).
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: Speculative decoding gains shrink at high batch sizes — big latency wins for interactive use, smaller throughput wins for bulk ingestion.
insights.locator: In the native single-pass benchmark on one H200

insights.claim: Fast parsing lets Nemotron Parse 3.5 use multi-pass extraction — re-parsing cropped tables/charts at higher detail (double pass) or adding a detection-mode verification pass (triple pass) — which adds 2.18 and 2.46 ParseBench points over single pass at the cost of throughput.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: Inference speed gains get reinvested into accuracy via test-time compute, supporting continued GPU demand per document.
insights.locator: Fast parsing gives us room to revisit difficult regions

insights.claim: NVIDIA released a Nemotron Parse fine-tuning recipe covering paired data generation, NeMo Automodel SFT, and NeMo RL GRPO using vLLM for candidate generation; users supply image/label pairs and a verifier built from reward components for text fidelity, bounding boxes, tables, chart facts and completion.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is packaging RLVR tooling to make enterprise domain-adaptation run on its NeMo software stack — software lock-in around its hardware.
insights.locator: Apply the same SFT/RLVR approach to your documents

insights.claim: In NVIDIA's synthetic dental-form (odontogram) example, sampled pass@1 rose from 0.00% for the base Nemotron Parse model to 95.85% after SFT and 96.58% after RLVR on 256 held-out forms.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: Small domain fine-tunes can take niche document types from unusable to production-grade; most of the gain comes from SFT, with RLVR adding a modest increment.
insights.locator: RLVR then reinforces accuracy and consistent completion

insights.claim: The community has already extended Nemotron Parse to Thai, Persian/Farsi and Arabic, and NVIDIA positions the new open datasets and recipes to accelerate such adaptations.
insights.speaker: Ryan Chesler
insights.so_what: Open-model community adoption broadens NVIDIA's ecosystem reach into non-English document markets.
insights.locator: We are excited that the community has extended
